definitions.explanation: A written symbol representing a sound or meaning, including hiragana, katakana, kanji, and letters from other writing systems.

examples.english: How do you read this character?

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{字|じ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦きれいで→きれい：00717_kirei⟧⟦{読|よ}みやすい→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: The teacher's handwriting is neat and easy to read.

examples.japanese: ⟦もっと→もっと：00798_motto⟧⟦{大|おお}きい→大きい：00335_ookii⟧{字|じ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}いて→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。⟦{小|ちい}さい→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{読|よ}めません→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: Please write in bigger characters. I can't read them if they're small.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{字|じ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}っていた→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{勉強|べんきょう}したら→勉強する：00527_benkyousuru⟧、⟦だんだん→だんだん：00832_dandan⟧⟦{読|よ}める→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦ように→よう：01114_you⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I used to think Japanese characters were hard, but after studying every day, I gradually became able to read them.

notes:
{字|じ} refers to written characters of any type.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {字|じ}を{書|か}く: to write characters
- {字|じ}を{読|よ}む: to read characters
- {字|じ}が{上手|じょうず}/{下手|へた}: good/bad handwriting
- {漢字|かんじ}: Chinese characters (kanji)
- ローマ{字|じ}: Roman letters

RELATED TERMS:
- {文字|もじ}: character, letter (more formal)
- ひらがな: hiragana
- カタカナ: katakana
- {漢字|かんじ}: kanji

Note: When talking about handwriting quality, {字|じ} often refers to how nicely someone writes.
